turn.speaker: Avery Chen
turn.text: Attendance is decisive here. Sunday afternoon has all 8 members free versus 4 on Saturday morning, and the room is available both days. Given the stated priority, I vote Sunday afternoon.

turn.speaker: Mira Patel
turn.text: Sunday afternoon maximizes participation with 8 available members. Since attendance outranks personal preference, that is the best choice on the supplied evidence.

turn.speaker: Dante Okafor
turn.text: I initially favor Saturday morning only as a minority-preservation check, but the prompt explicitly says prioritize attendance. With half the turnout, Saturday is weaker.

turn.text: Is there any evidence that Saturday’s smaller turnout offers a compensating advantage? I don’t see one. If not, the attendance rule seems to settle this cleanly.

turn.speaker: Avery Chen
turn.text: No compensating advantage is provided. Since the room and venue constraint are equal, the only supported distinction is attendance, which favors Sunday afternoon.

turn.speaker: Priya Sato
turn.text: Your Saturday preference lacks an evidence-based benefit under the stated criteria. Can it survive when attendance is the primary rule and the room availability is equal?

turn.speaker: Dante Okafor
turn.text: No. With only 4 free on Saturday and 8 on Sunday, the minority case is not strong enough under the prompt’s priority order. I withdraw Saturday as a serious competing recommendation.

turn.speaker: Noah Kim
turn.text: Constraint check passes: no paid venue is needed, and the same free room works both days. That removes non-attendance reasons to choose Saturday.

turn.speaker: Lina Morales
turn.text: Sunday afternoon is also more inclusive because it lets all 8 attend. Choosing Saturday would exclude half the group without any stated offsetting benefit.

turn.speaker: Jonas Reed
turn.text: From a convenience lens, both options use the same room, so convenience does not break the tie. Attendance does, and Sunday is plainly easier for the group as a whole.

turn.speaker: Elena Torres
turn.text: The failure case would be hidden constraints, but none are supplied. Under the given facts, there is no rational basis to prefer the lower-attendance slot.

turn.speaker: Zara Ndlovu
turn.text: Final vote confirmed: Sunday afternoon. The record is simple—same room, no paid venue, all 8 available. That meets the attendance-first rule most cleanly.

turn.speaker: Avery Chen
turn.text: Final verdict: Sunday afternoon. Majority reasoning is unanimous by the end because the supplied evidence strongly favors the higher-attendance option under the stated criteria.
